subject: Engineering Mechanics
summary: free-body diagrams, equilibrium, trusses and frames, and friction

questions.text: Three coplanar forces act at a point: 50 N along the +x axis, 80 N at 60° and 60 N at 150° (angles measured anticlockwise from +x). The magnitude of their resultant is
solution: Concept: Resolve every force into x and y components, add them, then combine.
Exam tip: 190 N is the arithmetic sum, a common trap. Forces add as vectors, never as numbers.

questions.text: A 1000 N lamp is hung from two cables as shown. Cable A makes 45° and cable B makes 30° with the vertical. The tension in cable B (in N) is ______
solution: Concept: Three concurrent forces in equilibrium. Write ΣFx = 0 and ΣFy = 0 (or use Lami's theorem).
Horizontal: T<sub>A</sub> sin 45° = T<sub>B</sub> sin 30° → T<sub>A</sub> = 0.7071 T<sub>B</sub>
Vertical: T<sub>A</sub> cos 45° + T<sub>B</sub> cos 30° = 1000 → 0.5 T<sub>B</sub> + 0.866 T<sub>B</sub> = 1000
Exam tip: The cable closer to the vertical always carries more load.

questions.text: A 200 N force is applied at the end of a 0.5 m spanner, making 60° with the handle. The moment about the bolt centre is
solution: Concept: Moment = force × perpendicular distance, or use only the force component perpendicular to the arm (Varignon's theorem).
Perpendicular component = 200 sin 60° = 173.2 N
Exam tip: 100 N·m would be correct only if the force were at 90° to the handle.

questions.text: The simply supported beam AB carries a 20 kN point load and a 5 kN/m UDL as shown. The reaction at support B (in kN) is ______
solution: Concept: Replace the UDL by its resultant at the centre of its length, then take moments about A.
UDL resultant = 5 × 2 = 10 kN, acting at 5 m from A.
ΣMA = 0: RB × 6 = 20 × 2 + 10 × 5 = 90 → RB = 15 kN
ΣFy = 0: RA = 30 − 15 = 15 kN
Exam tip: Always check the second reaction with ΣFy = 0; it catches arithmetic slips.

questions.text: The truss shown carries a single load of 40 kN at joint L2. L0 is a pin and L3 is a roller. Which member is a zero-force member?
solution: Concept: If three members meet at an unloaded joint and two of them are collinear, the third member carries zero force.
At joint L1, members L0L1 and L1L2 are collinear (both horizontal) and no load acts at L1.
So ΣFy = 0 at L1 gives FU1L1 = 0.
U2L2 is not zero, because the 40 kN load acts at L2.
Exam tip: Spot zero-force members first. They shrink the problem before you write any equation.

questions.text: For the same truss (40 kN at L2), the force in the top chord member U1U2 (magnitude, in kN) is ______  Also state whether it is tension or compression.
solution: Concept: Method of sections. Cut through U1U2, U1L2 and L1L2 (section 1–1) and take moments about the point where two of the cut members meet.
Reactions: RL0 = 40 × 3/9 = 13.33 kN, RL3 = 26.67 kN.
Left part, moments about L2 (where U1L2 and L1L2 meet): R<sub>L0</sub> × 6 + F<sub>U1U2</sub> × 3 = 0, taking F as tension.
FU1U2 = −13.33 × 6 / 3 = −26.67 kN → 26.67 kN compression.
Exam tip: The top chord of a simply supported truss under downward loads is always in compression; the bottom chord is in tension.

questions.text: A 500 N block on a rough horizontal floor (μ = 0.3) is pulled by a force P inclined at θ above the horizontal. The least value of P that can start the motion, and the angle at which it acts, are
solution: Concept: P cos θ = μ(W − P sin θ) → P = μW / (cos θ + μ sin θ). P is least when the denominator is greatest, i.e. when tan θ = μ (θ equals the angle of friction).
Exam tip: Pulling slightly upward beats a horizontal pull (150 N) because it reduces the normal reaction.

questions.text: A 400 N block rests on a rough plane inclined at 25° (μ = 0.2). The horizontal force P needed to just push it up the plane (in N) is ______
solution: Concept: With the angle of friction φ = tan⁻¹μ, a horizontal force to push a block up an incline is P = W tan(α + φ).
Check by components: along the plane P cos α = W sin α + μN, with N = W cos α + P sin α. Solving gives the same 293.9 N.
Exam tip: A horizontal push also presses the block into the plane, which increases friction. That is why it needs more force than a push along the plane.

questions.text: A uniform ladder rests against a rough vertical wall and on a rough floor, with μ = 0.25 at both surfaces. The least angle the ladder can make with the floor without slipping is
solution: Concept: At impending slip both friction forces reach their limits: Ff = μNf (towards the wall) and Fw = μNw (upwards).
ΣF<sub>x</sub>: N<sub>w</sub> = μN<sub>f</sub>. ΣF<sub>y</sub>: N<sub>f</sub> + μN<sub>w</sub> = W → N<sub>f</sub> = W/(1 + μ²)
ΣM about the foot: N<sub>w</sub> L sin θ + μN<sub>w</sub> L cos θ = W (L/2) cos θ
Exam tip: With a smooth wall the formula becomes tan θ = 1/(2μ) = 2, giving 63.4°. Wall friction lets the ladder stand slightly flatter.

questions.text: A rope passes half-way round a fixed rough cylinder (μ = 0.3) and is used to raise a load of 500 N slowly. The pull needed on the other end (in N) is ______
solution: Concept: Belt (capstan) friction: T1/T2 = eμθ, with T1 the tight side and θ in radians.
θ = π rad (half turn), so e<sup>0.3π</sup> = e<sup>0.9425</sup> = 2.566
To raise the load, the pull is on the tight side: T1 = 500 × 2.566 = 1283 N
Exam tip: To lower the load slowly, the same cylinder needs only 500/2.566 = 195 N. Always decide which side is tight first.

questions.text: Blocks A (200 N, μ = 0.2) and B (300 N, μ = 0.3) are tied together by a string parallel to an inclined plane, with A below B. The angle of inclination (in degrees) at which the pair just begins to slide down is ______
solution: Concept: When connected bodies slide together, total driving force = total limiting friction.
Driving force = (200 + 300) sin α = 500 sin α
Total friction = (0.2 × 200 + 0.3 × 300) cos α = 130 cos α
Exam tip: Neither block alone sets the angle (A alone would slide at 11.3°, B alone at 16.7°). The string makes them share friction.

questions.text: A light horizontal beam AB, hinged to the wall at A, is held by a cable BC at 30° to the beam. It carries 6 kN at mid-span and 4 kN at B. The tension in the cable is
solution: Concept: Take moments about the hinge A so that both unknown hinge reactions drop out.
Vertical component of T at B = T sin 30°, acting at 4 m from A.
Hinge reaction: Ax = T cos 30° = 12.12 kN, Ay = 10 − 7 = 3 kN → RA = 12.49 kN
Exam tip: The cable is a two-force member, so its tension acts along the cable. Use that direction directly.

questions.text: For the wall-mounted truss shown, with 20 kN hanging at C, the force in member AC is
solution: Concept: Method of joints at C, the joint with only two unknown members.
BC has slope 2/3, so sin α = 2/√13 and cos α = 3/√13.
ΣFy at C: FBC sin α = 20 → FBC = 36.06 kN, pushing C upward (compression).
ΣFx at C: FAC = FBC cos α = 36.06 × 3/√13 = 30 kN tension
Exam tip: In a wall bracket the upper member is in tension (it is pulled) and the lower strut is in compression (it is pushed).

questions.text: A uniform block 0.4 m wide and 1.0 m tall stands on a plane whose inclination α is slowly increased. If μ = 0.5, the block will
solution: Concept: Compare two limits. Sliding starts when tan α = μ. Tipping starts when the weight's line of action passes the lower edge, i.e. tan α = b/h.
Sliding: tan α = 0.5 → α = 26.6°
Tipping: tan α = 0.4/1.0 → α = 21.8°
The smaller angle is reached first, so the block tips over at 21.8° before it can slide.
Exam tip: Tall, narrow bodies tip; short, wide bodies slide. Always check both.

questions.text: A roller of weight 1000 N and radius 0.5 m is to be pulled over a step 0.2 m high by a horizontal force P through its centre. The least P needed (in N) is ______
solution: Concept: At the moment of lifting, the floor reaction becomes zero. The roller then has three forces (P, W and the step reaction R), and R passes through the centre.
Take moments about the step corner. Lever arm of W = √(r² − (r − h)²) = √(0.25 − 0.09) = 0.4 m. Lever arm of P = r − h = 0.3 m.
Exam tip: P = W√(h(2r − h))/(r − h). As h approaches r the force becomes infinite, which is why a horizontal pull cannot lift a roller over a step as high as its radius.
